posts: The CLARITY Act cloture vote failed 49–50 yesterday. Eleven short of 60 — and one short of even a simple majority. But "crypto has no rules now" is the wrong takeaway, and the right one is more interesting 🧵
1/ It didn't break on the SEC/CFTC market-structure framework. It broke on ethics language covering officials' crypto holdings. No voting Democrat backed the motion; four Republicans opposed it.

2/ Meanwhile the agencies didn't wait. SEC: Project Crypto, a token taxonomy, and a proposed Regulation Crypto Assets offering regime (Aug 18) — which the SEC says is partly meant to reduce the incentive to organize offshore.

3/ CFTC went further in practice. Listed spot crypto began trading on federally regulated US markets in Dec 2025, DCMs can list spot including leveraged retail, and a joint March 2026 taxonomy named 16 assets as digital commodities.

4/ So why does a law still matter? Because a rule and a statute can say identical things and be worth different amounts. A commission can supersede a rule. A court can vacate it. Congress can disapprove it. A proposal can just never be finalized.

5/ That's what capital is pricing. A ten-year fund underwrites a regime across a horizon longer than any administration — and guidance a successor could withdraw gets discounted. New VC fund formation just hit its lowest quarterly total since 2020.

6/ Same for founders. Jurisdiction is a multi-year, hard-to-reverse bet made against the rules you expect at exit, not the rules today. That's why offshore structuring survived a friendlier Washington.

7/ The part most worth writing into law: self-custody. 1.3B adults have no financial account. 86% own a phone. That gap isn't technology — it's permission. A self-custodial wallet is an account nobody has to grant you.

8/ And it's already happening: $33T of stablecoin transfers settled on public chains in 2025 (+72% y/y), 71% of LatAm firms using them for cross-border settlement, while Sub-Saharan remittances still cost 6%+.

9/ Which makes Section 604 the real stake — whether publishing non-custodial code makes you a money transmitter. Settled in guidance it can be resettled. Leaving it open doesn't protect anyone; it just exports the work. https://www.swopme.co/blog/clarity-act-vote-explained
